doc.title: Howard Levy interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 11, 2025

title: A typical month: touring, Chicago gigs and composing
summary: Levy says he has no typical month; he alternates tours with few Chicago gigs, using free time to compose, and recently wrote a second concerto.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: I was looking at my own calendar today and thinking well all musicians have to have a calendar, whether it hangs on the refrigerator or it’s in your phone. Can you describe to me what a typical month is like for you? What does your calendar look like?

That’s a very interesting story. I mean an old musician’s joke is, “Hey man, my calendar looks like snow, you know, so – I don’t have a typical month. It just all depends on what I’m up to. During the course of my life I’ve had so many different types of careers so sometimes I might be on tour for a month, and sometimes I might be home for a month with just like two or three gigs in Chicago because I live in the Chicago area. And I try not to overexpose myself here. You know I have a certain status I’ve achieved here so I try to pick my spots that make the maximum impact. And sometimes when I don’t have that many actual gigs happening, those are the times that I use to compose and write. Because I just wrote my second concerto for myself. Actually I did that last year. And I deliberately left some time free where I wasn’t taking – I tried to take as few gigs as possible to be able to, you know, concentrate on composing this concerto, which I knew would take, you know like total immersion. And I also just put out my musical memoirs.
